opportunities.gap: The Transfer Case (line 109) asserts as fact that text-to-image models 'default to stereotyped depictions of role, gender, age, and ethnicity.' This is a load-bearing empirical claim and the course's own currency-watch flags that any model-specific claim about bias behavior must be verified against current (2026) text-to-image models, which have undergone substantial debiasing/RLHF and prompt-rewriting interventions since the early diffusion era. The claim is asserted with no citation and may overstate or misdate the behavior.
opportunities.proposed_change: Soften and ground the claim: cite a specific audited finding (e.g., Bianchi et al. 2023 on Stable Diffusion stereotype amplification; Luccioni et al. 2023 Stable Bias) and add a hedge noting that 2024-2026 commercial models apply prompt-rewriting and debiasing that reduce but do not eliminate the effect, so a representation audit is still required. Keep the pedagogical point (audit for social accuracy) but attach a real source and a current-state qualifier.
opportunities.where_to_apply: 03.mdx — 'Transfer Case' section, the sentence 'the model defaults to stereotyped depictions of role, gender, age, and ethnicity'
search_terms: DALL-E Midjourney debiasing prompt rewriting representation 2024

opportunities.gap: The Core Concept and Decision Rule reference 'a WCAG requirement' only generically, and the References list omits WCAG entirely despite this being a WCAG-centric section. For a 2026 graduate LXD course the standard should be pinned to a specific version and the two governing success criteria named, with a note on WCAG 3.0's draft (not yet Recommendation) status.
opportunities.proposed_change: Pin the standard to WCAG 2.2 AA (W3C Recommendation since Oct 2023, still current in 2026) and cite the two governing success criteria by number: SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (the alt obligation) and SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (the color-only prohibition). Add a one-line note that WCAG 3.0 remains an early W3C Working Draft (Candidate Rec not expected until ~2027-2028, final ~2028-2030), so 2.2 AA is the operative target. Add a WCAG 2.2 entry to the References list (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/).
opportunities.where_to_apply: 05.mdx — Core Concept (third decision 'a WCAG requirement') and Decision Rule step 3; add to References list

opportunities.gap: The References list cites UDL via a bare generic link (udlguidelines.cast.org) with no version. A 2026 course citing 'UDL learner variability' as a core anchor should reference 3.0.
opportunities.proposed_change: Update the References UDL entry to 'CAST (2024). Universal Design for Learning Guidelines version 3.0. https://udlguidelines.cast.org/'.
